title: Sequenced compatibility and comms cadence for model-tagging version rollout
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: roll out a model-tagging-based versioning layer that lets customers opt into v2 behavior while keeping stable support for v1 for 90 days. This ticket coordinates the cross-functional launch plan: release notes cadence, migration guides, breaking-change warnings in Console/API, SDK compatibility shims, and GTM comms to partners and pilot customers. We will stage the rollout in three waves: internal canary, beta opt-in, and public default switch-over. The scope includes docs, SDK changes, console UX (version selector + migration warnings), release notes templates, support runbook updates, and telemetry to measure migration progress and quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Public migration guide published and linked from Console and API docs
SDKs (Python, JS, Go) expose a stable 'model_tag' parameter with backward-compatible defaults
Console shows per-route version selector and a non-blocking migration warning for v1 routes
Release notes for hosted API, Dedicated, and Private include clear timeline and rollback instructions
Support runbook and escalation matrix updated; at least two support engineers and one on-call PM trained
Telemetry captures: percent of requests using v2 tags, error delta vs baseline, latency delta vs baseline
tasks: Docs: Draft migration guide + quickstart examples for common patterns (chat, embeddings, rerank)
SDKs: Add model_tag param, deprecation warnings, and integration tests; publish patch releases
Console: Add version selector component, migration banner, and link to migration guide
API: Add response header 'x-redwood-model-version' and warning payload for deprecated routes
Runtime/ENG: Add compatibility layer that maps model_tag to runtime variant; feature flag for canary
Release notes: Create canonical release note template and per-channel snippets (docs site, changelog, email)
GTM: Draft partner comms, customer playbook, and support FAQs
Observability: Dashboard and alerts for error & latency regressions during rollout
Legal/Compliance: Review DPA/KMS implications for behavior changes and document approvals
Migration tooling: Build a 'migration-check' script customers can run to validate prompts against v2
rollout_timeline: 2026-03-10: Internal canary deploy (1% traffic) behind feature flag; invite Platform and SEs to validate
2026-03-17: Beta opt-in open to customers via Console toggle; announce to pilot program participants

2026-04-01: Release notes and blog post announcing scheduled public default change window
2026-04-10: Start 7-day public preview period where new accounts default to v2 but existing keep v1
2026-04-17: Public default switch-over (customers will be notified 7 days prior); provide rollback policy
2026-05-17: End-of-support for v1 (90 days after switch-over); final deprecation notice and archived docs
notification_matrix: Pilot customers: email + direct Slack (account team) one week before beta opens
All customers: blog post and docs site at beta start; console banner for affected routes
Enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private): Account managers and Solutions Engineers 3 weeks prior + separate migration workshop
Marketplace partners: partner portal announcement and PR contact
Internal engineering: #infra-alerts for canary metrics; weekly sync with runtime owners
Support: triage playbook pushed to internal KB and 2-hour training session before public preview
migration_checklist: Run 'migration-check' against production prompt set and record quality metrics
Pin critical routes to v1 if regression delta > 2% on key evals
Add response header checks in integration tests to ensure version visibility
Update IaC templates if customers use model aliases/route pinning
Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams for in-place upgrade notes and offline upgrade windows

notes_for_review: Tradeoffs: We prefer opt-in beta to reduce risk, but opt-in slows migration uptake. Consider incentives (eg. credits) for pilot participants.
Fallback policy: If v2 regressions exceed thresholds during canary, automated rollback to previous runtime variant will occur; need runbook detail from ENG
Telemetry baseline: Use 14-day rolling baseline prior to canary start for error/latency comparisons
Risk areas: embeddings/long-context models show higher variance on initial tests; plan additional eval suites for these workloads
